disclaimer: Archetypes are original PersonalityDNA descriptive summaries of trait patterns. They are not validated psychological types; most people show elements of several archetypes.
method: Each Big Five score is centred: d = (score - 50) / 50, giving -1..1. Each archetype has a prototype of +1, -1 or 0 per trait. Fit = sum(p * d) / sqrt(number of non-zero prototype traits). The two highest fits are the primary and secondary archetypes; ties break by the order below. If the best fit is below weak_fit_threshold the profile is labelled 'balanced' and the archetypes are shown as a weak fit.

archetypes.name: The Strategist
archetypes.summary: Tends to combine big-picture thinking with structured planning, and is often comfortable making candid calls.
growth: Invite input before deciding
Explain the reasoning behind decisions to others

archetypes.name: The Visionary
archetypes.summary: Tends to generate new possibilities, share them energetically and stay composed when plans change.
growth: Pair ideas with concrete next steps
Check that others have capacity before adding new goals

archetypes.name: The Innovator
archetypes.summary: Tends to favour experimentation and flexible approaches over fixed routines.
growth: Build light routines that protect follow-through
Finish one experiment before starting the next

archetypes.name: The Analyst
archetypes.summary: Tends to enjoy careful, independent work on complex ideas with attention to detail.
growth: Share work in progress earlier
Decide when 'good enough' is sufficient

archetypes.name: The Explorer
archetypes.summary: Tends to seek new experiences, people and places, and enjoys spontaneity.
growth: Keep a simple record of commitments
Revisit goals before moving to the next new thing

archetypes.name: The Organizer
archetypes.summary: Tends to value proven methods, order and dependable routines.
growth: Try one small new approach at a time
Ask what problem a proposed change is solving

archetypes.name: The Advocate
archetypes.summary: Tends to champion ideas and people, combining warmth with an interest in change.
growth: Protect time for your own priorities
Check assumptions with people you are advocating for

archetypes.name: The Connector
archetypes.summary: Tends to enjoy meeting people and helping them feel welcome and linked to one another.
growth: Make room for quieter voices
Say no to requests that stretch you too thin

archetypes.name: The Diplomat
archetypes.summary: Tends to stay calm and considerate in tense moments and look for common ground.
growth: State your own view clearly, even when it differs
Address issues early rather than smoothing them over

archetypes.name: The Builder
archetypes.summary: Tends to get practical things done with energy, structure and a preference for what works.
growth: Leave space to reconsider the approach
Notice when others need more time to adjust

archetypes.name: The Mentor
archetypes.summary: Tends to offer steady, dependable support and enjoys helping others grow.
growth: Let others find their own answers sometimes
Ask for support yourself

archetypes.name: The Investigator
archetypes.summary: Tends to explore questions quietly and thoroughly, staying even-tempered while doing so.
growth: Share findings in a form others can use
Set limits on open-ended exploration

archetypes.name: The Creator
archetypes.summary: Tends to follow imaginative ideas in a personal, unhurried way.
growth: Set gentle deadlines for creative work
Show work to trusted people for feedback

archetypes.name: The Collaborator
archetypes.summary: Tends to value cooperation and practical, familiar ways of working with others.
growth: Share your ideas, not only support for others' ideas
Stay open to unfamiliar approaches

archetypes.name: The Independent Thinker
archetypes.summary: Tends to form views independently and is comfortable questioning consensus.
growth: Explain your reasoning so others can follow it
Seek out views that challenge your own

archetypes.name: The Motivator
archetypes.summary: Tends to bring upbeat, steady energy that encourages others to keep going.
growth: Acknowledge setbacks honestly
Listen before encouraging
